## Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, Milan

<!-- Last updated: 2026-02-04 -->

- [Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galleria_Vittorio_Emanuele_II)
  - **Type**: Historic Shopping Arcade
  - **Description**: Italy's oldest active shopping arcade and a major landmark of Milan. Housed within a four-story double arcade in the centre of town, the Galleria was designed in 1861 and built by architect Giuseppe Mengoni between 1865 and 1877. Named after Victor Emmanuel II, the first king of the Kingdom of Italy.

### Artists

- [Giuseppe Mengoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giuseppe_Mengoni)
  - **Born**: 1829, Fontanelice
  - **Died**: 1877, Milan
  - Italian architect who designed the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II in Milan, one of the largest and most impressive iron-and-glass covered arcades of the 19th century. The project was the first example of a monumentally scaled iron and steel arcade in Italy, executed in a Renaissance Revival style.

## La Rinascente, Milan

<!-- Last updated: 2026-02-04 -->

- [La Rinascente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Rinascente)
  - **Type**: Department Store
  - **Description**: A high-end Italian department store chain founded in Milan in 1865. The current name was coined by the poet Gabriele D'Annunzio in 1917. In 1954, the company launched the Compasso d'Oro, an Italian industrial design award. In 2016, its Milan store at Piazza del Duomo was named "Best Department Store in the World" by the IGDS.

## Doge's Palace, Venice

<!-- Last updated: 2026-02-04 -->

- [Doge's Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doge's_Palace)
  - **Type**: Palace / Museum
  - **Description**: A palace built in Venetian Gothic style and one of the main landmarks of Venice. The palace included government offices, a jail, and the residence of the Doge of Venice. Originally built in 810, rebuilt in 1340 and extended in following centuries. It became a museum in 1923 and is one of 11 museums run by the Fondazione Musei Civici di Venezia.

### Artworks

- [Il Paradiso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il_Paradiso)
  - **Artist**: [Tintoretto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tintoretto)
  - **Medium**: Oil on canvas
  - **Date**: 1588-1592
  - **Description**: A massive painting (22 x 9 metres) dominating the main hall of the Doge's Palace, one of the largest paintings on canvas in the world. The composition features around 500 figures in a heavenly scene. The light emanating from Christ descends along the central axis directly to the doge's throne, symbolizing that the Doge receives his authority from on high.

- The Rape of Europa
  - **Artist**: [Paolo Veronese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Veronese)
  - **Medium**: Oil on canvas
  - **Date**: c. 1580
  - **Description**: Located in the Sala dell'Anticollegio, this mythological painting depicts the abduction of Europa by Zeus in the form of a white bull. It hangs alongside Tintoretto's allegories.

- Apotheosis of Venice
  - **Artist**: [Paolo Veronese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Veronese)
  - **Medium**: Oil on canvas (ceiling)
  - **Date**: 1585
  - **Description**: A ceiling painting in the Chamber of the Great Council celebrating Venice personified, surrounded by allegorical figures representing Peace, Justice, and Fame. A masterpiece of illusionistic ceiling painting.

- Juno Showering Gifts on Venice
  - **Artist**: [Paolo Veronese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Veronese)
  - **Medium**: Oil on canvas (ceiling)
  - **Date**: 1553-1554
  - **Description**: Located in the Council of Ten Room, this ceiling painting shows the goddess Juno bestowing gifts upon the personification of Venice, symbolizing the city's prosperity and divine favor.

### Artists

- [Tintoretto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tintoretto)
  - **Born**: 1518, Venice
  - **Died**: 1594, Venice
  - Jacopo Robusti, known as Tintoretto, was an Italian Renaissance painter of the Venetian school. His contemporaries both admired and criticized the speed with which he painted and the unprecedented boldness of his brushwork. For his phenomenal energy in painting he was termed "il Furioso." His work is characterized by muscular figures, dramatic gestures and bold use of perspective.

- [Paolo Veronese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Veronese)
  - **Born**: 1528, Verona
  - **Died**: 1588, Venice
  - Italian Renaissance painter based in Venice, known for extremely large history paintings of religion and mythology. With Titian and Tintoretto, Veronese is one of the "great trio that dominated Venetian painting of the cinquecento." Known as a supreme colorist who developed a naturalist style influenced by Titian.

## Saint Mark's Basilica, Venice

<!-- Last updated: 2026-02-04 -->

- [St Mark's Basilica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Mark's_Basilica)
  - **Type**: Cathedral / Basilica
  - **Description**: The Patriarchal Cathedral Basilica of Saint Mark is the cathedral church of the Patriarchate of Venice. It became the episcopal seat in 1807, replacing San Pietro di Castello. Dedicated to and holding the relics of Saint Mark the Evangelist, the patron saint of Venice. One of the finest examples of Byzantine architecture, renowned for its golden mosaics.

### Artworks

- [Pala d'Oro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pala_d'Oro)
  - **Artist**: Byzantine craftsmen
  - **Medium**: Gold, enamel, precious gems
  - **Date**: 10th-14th century (created in phases)
  - **Description**: The high altar retable of the Basilica, universally recognized as one of the most refined works of Byzantine enamel. Adorned with 1,927 precious gems including 526 pearls, 330 garnets, 320 emeralds, 255 sapphires, and 75 rubies. The jewel-encrusted altarpiece depicts scenes from the life of Christ and took 366 years to complete.
  ![img](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/92/Venise%2C_Pala_d%27Oro_expos%C3%A9e.JPG)

- [Horses of Saint Mark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horses_of_Saint_Mark)
  - **Artist**: Unknown (possibly Greek or Roman)
  - **Medium**: Bronze with gold gilding
  - **Date**: Antiquity (possibly 4th century BC or 2nd century AD)
  - **Description**: A group of four bronze horses that originally formed part of a quadriga monument. Brought to Venice from Constantinople after the Fourth Crusade in 1204. The originals are now in the basilica museum, with replicas on the facade. Also known as the Triumphal Quadriga.
  ![img](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/bb/Horses_of_Basilica_San_Marco_bright.jpg)

- Byzantine Mosaics
  - **Artist**: Various Byzantine and Venetian craftsmen
  - **Medium**: Gold and glass mosaic
  - **Date**: 11th-13th century (and later)
  - **Description**: The basilica features 8,000 square meters of mosaics illuminating the interior. The oldest surviving mosaic, depicting Saint Alipio, dates to 1260 and shows the translation of Saint Mark's relics from Alexandria, with merchants hiding the body beneath pork to avoid Muslim inspection.

### Bible Stories

- [Translation of Relics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Translation_(relics))
  - **Book(s)**: Church tradition
  - **Description**: The mosaic over the first portal depicts the legendary theft of Saint Mark's body from Alexandria in 828 by Venetian merchants Rustico and Bruno, who hid it beneath pork to avoid Muslim guards.

## St Mark's Campanile, Venice

<!-- Last updated: 2026-02-04 -->

- [St Mark's Campanile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Mark's_Campanile)
  - **Type**: Bell Tower
  - **Description**: The bell tower of St Mark's Basilica in Venice. At 98.6 metres in height, it is the tallest structure in Venice and is colloquially termed "el paron de casa" (the master of the house). The current structure is a reconstruction completed in 1912, the previous tower having collapsed in 1902.

## Piazza San Marco, Venice

<!-- Last updated: 2026-02-04 -->

- [Piazza San Marco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_San_Marco)
  - **Type**: Public Square
  - **Description**: The principal public square of Venice, generally known just as "la Piazza." The Piazzetta extends toward the San Marco basin. Together they form the social, religious and political centre of Venice. The square is flanked by the Basilica, the Doge's Palace, the Campanile, and the Procuratie buildings.

## Bridge of Sighs, Venice

<!-- Last updated: 2026-02-04 -->

- [Bridge of Sighs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridge_of_Sighs)
  - **Type**: Bridge
  - **Description**: An enclosed bridge made of white limestone with windows featuring stone bars. It passes over the Rio di Palazzo and connects the New Prison to the interrogation rooms in the Doge's Palace. Designed by Antonio Contin (whose uncle Antonio da Ponte designed the Rialto Bridge) and built in 1600. Named for the sighs of prisoners who crossed it on their way to execution.

### Artists

- Antonio Contin
  - **Born**: Unknown
  - **Died**: c. 1600
  - Italian architect who designed the Bridge of Sighs. His uncle Antonio da Ponte designed the famous Rialto Bridge. Both bridges are iconic landmarks of Venice.

## Palazzo Contarini del Bovolo, Venice

- [Palazzo Contarini del Bovolo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palazzo_Contarini_del_Bovolo)

  - **Description**: A small palazzo in Venice best known for its external multi-arch spiral staircase known as the Scala Contarini del Bovolo. ## Basilica di Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari, Venice

<!-- Last updated: 2026-02-04 -->

- [Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Maria_Gloriosa_dei_Frari)
  - **Type**: Church / Minor Basilica
  - **Description**: Commonly known as the Frari, this church is located in the Campo dei Frari at the heart of the San Polo district. One of the largest churches in Venice and one of the few surviving Gothic churches. Dedicated to the Assumption of Mary. Contains masterpieces by Titian, Giovanni Bellini, and Donatello in their original settings.

### Artworks

- [Assumption of the Virgin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_of_the_Virgin_(Titian))
  - **Artist**: [Titian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian)
  - **Medium**: Oil on panel
  - **Date**: 1515-1518
  - **Description**: Titian's most famous painting, commissioned for the Basilica and remaining in its original position on the high altar. The largest altarpiece in Venice, with figures well over life-size. The work established Titian as the most prominent painter of 16th century Venice. Also known as the Assunta.
  ![img](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9e/Tizian_041.jpg)

- [Pesaro Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pesaro_Madonna)
  - **Artist**: [Titian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian)
  - **Medium**: Oil on canvas
  - **Date**: 1519-1526
  - **Description**: Located in the left nave, this revolutionary painting places the Madonna and Child dramatically off-center to the upper right rather than in the physical center. Commissioned by Bishop Jacopo Pesaro, this asymmetrical arrangement was highly innovative and influenced religious painting for generations.
  ![img](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b8/Frari_%28Venice%29_nave_left_-_Altar_of_Madona_di_Ca%27Pesaro.jpg)

- [Frari Triptych](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frari_Triptych)
  - **Artist**: [Giovanni Bellini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovanni_Bellini)
  - **Medium**: Oil on panel
  - **Date**: 1488
  - **Description**: Also called the Pesaro Triptych, this masterpiece hangs in the sacristy. Signed and dated on the Virgin Mary's throne. One of Bellini's finest works showing the Madonna and Child with Saints Nicholas of Bari, Peter, Mark, and Benedict. The three-dimensional effect is astonishing.
  ![img](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/0d/Frari_%28Venice%29_-_Sacristy_-_triptych_by_Giovanni_Bellini.jpg)

- [Saint John the Baptist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_John_the_Baptist_(Donatello))
  - **Artist**: [Donatello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donatello)
  - **Medium**: Painted wood
  - **Date**: 1438
  - **Description**: The only statue by Donatello still in Venice. This wooden sculpture was restored in 1973, revealing the artist's signature with the date 1438. Located in the Cappella di San Giovanni Battista.
  ![img](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/8d/Frari_%28Venice%29_Cappella_di_San_Giovanni_Battista_-_San_Giovanni_Battista_di_Donatello.jpg)

- Monument to Titian
  - **Artist**: Luigi Zandomeneghi and others
  - **Medium**: Marble
  - **Date**: 1852
  - **Description**: A large 19th-century monument marking Titian's burial place, including a relief version of the Assumption. Titian died of plague in 1576 and was buried here despite plague regulations normally requiring burial elsewhere.

- Tomb of Antonio Canova
  - **Artist**: [Antonio Canova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Canova) (design) and students
  - **Medium**: Marble
  - **Date**: 1827
  - **Description**: A pyramidal monument originally designed by Canova as a tomb for Titian. After Canova's death, his students used the design to create his own memorial. His heart is interred here; his body is in Possagno.

### Artists

- [Titian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian)
  - **Born**: c. 1488, Pieve di Cadore
  - **Died**: 1576, Venice
  - Tiziano Vecellio, known as Titian, was the most important artist of Renaissance Venetian painting. Buried in the Frari.

- [Giovanni Bellini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovanni_Bellini)
  - **Born**: c. 1430, Venice
  - **Died**: 1516, Venice
  - Italian Renaissance painter, probably the best known of the Bellini family of Venetian painters. His brother-in-law was Andrea Mantegna.

- [Donatello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donatello)
  - **Born**: c. 1386, Florence
  - **Died**: 1466, Florence
  - Donato di Niccolo di Betto Bardi, known as Donatello, was an Italian sculptor of the Renaissance period who developed an Early Renaissance style of sculpture. His David was the first freestanding nude male sculpture since antiquity.

- [Antonio Canova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Canova)
  - **Born**: 1757, Possagno
  - **Died**: 1822, Venice
  - Italian Neoclassical sculptor, famous for his marble sculptures. Often regarded as the greatest of the Neoclassical artists.

### Bible Stories

- [Assumption of Mary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_of_Mary)
  - **Book(s)**: Catholic doctrine
  - **Description**: The belief that Mary, mother of Jesus, was assumed bodily into Heaven at the end of her earthly life. The subject of the church's dedication and Titian's famous altarpiece.

## Santa Maria della Salute, Venice

<!-- Last updated: 2026-02-04 -->

- [Santa Maria della Salute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Maria_della_Salute)
  - **Type**: Church / Minor Basilica
  - **Description**: Commonly known as La Salute, this Roman Catholic church is located at Punta della Dogana in the Dorsoduro sestiere. Built as a votive offering for Venice's deliverance from the devastating plague of 1630. Designed in Baroque style by Baldassare Longhena, completed in 1687.

### Artworks

- [Saint Mark Enthroned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Mark_Enthroned)
  - **Artist**: [Titian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian)
  - **Medium**: Oil on panel
  - **Date**: 1510-1511
  - **Description**: The altarpiece of the sacristy, originally painted for Santo Spirito in Isola. Saint Mark sits enthroned holding his gospel, flanked by Saints Cosmas and Damian (patron saints of physicians) on the left, and Saints Roch and Sebastian (saints invoked during plague) on the right. Thought to be Titian's first independent commission.
  ![img](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3d/Titian_-_St_Mark_Enthroned_with_Saints_-_WGA22765.jpg)

- [David and Goliath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_and_Goliath_(Titian))
  - **Artist**: [Titian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian)
  - **Medium**: Oil on canvas (ceiling)
  - **Date**: 1542-1544
  - **Description**: One of three dramatic ceiling paintings, originally for Santo Spirito. Walter Friedlaender called these paintings "manifestations of genius unprecedented even in Titian's own work" for their impassioned power of movement and daring use of foreshortening. Highly influential on Baroque painting.
  ![img](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/56/Titian_-_David_and_Goliath_-_WGA22779.jpg)

- Abraham and Isaac
  - **Artist**: [Titian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian)
  - **Medium**: Oil on canvas (ceiling)
  - **Date**: 1542-1544
  - **Description**: Ceiling painting in the sacristy, part of the trio with David and Goliath and Cain and Abel. Depicts the moment of Abraham's sacrifice being stayed by an angel. Demonstrates Titian's mastery of dramatic perspective.

- Cain and Abel
  - **Artist**: [Titian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian)
  - **Medium**: Oil on canvas (ceiling)
  - **Date**: 1542-1544
  - **Description**: Ceiling painting showing Cain killing his brother Abel. Part of Titian's Old Testament ceiling series, renowned for its powerful foreshortening and dynamic composition.

- The Pentecost
  - **Artist**: [Titian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian)
  - **Medium**: Oil on canvas
  - **Date**: c. 1545
  - **Description**: A large painting in the nave depicting the descent of the Holy Spirit upon the apostles. One of several Titian works transferred to the Salute from suppressed churches.

- Marriage at Cana
  - **Artist**: [Tintoretto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tintoretto)
  - **Medium**: Oil on canvas
  - **Date**: 1561
  - **Description**: Displayed in the great sacristy, this painting depicts Christ's first miracle at the wedding feast. Notable for including a self-portrait of the artist among the wedding guests.

### Artists

- [Baldassare Longhena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baldassare_Longhena)
  - **Born**: 1598, Venice
  - **Died**: 1682, Venice
  - Italian architect, one of the greatest exponents of Baroque architecture in Venice. His style is characterized by monumentality, skillful use of light and shadow, and an understanding of Venetian aesthetics. The Salute is his masterpiece.

### Bible Stories

- [David and Goliath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_and_Goliath)
  - **Book(s)**: 1 Samuel
  - **Chapters/Verses**: 1 Samuel 17
  - **Description**: The story of the young shepherd David defeating the Philistine giant Goliath with a sling and stone. A symbol of triumph through faith over seemingly insurmountable odds.

- [Binding of Isaac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binding_of_Isaac)
  - **Book(s)**: Genesis
  - **Chapters/Verses**: Genesis 22:1-19
  - **Description**: God tests Abraham by commanding him to sacrifice his son Isaac. An angel stops Abraham at the last moment, and a ram is sacrificed instead. Prefigures Christ's sacrifice.

- [Cain and Abel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cain_and_Abel)
  - **Book(s)**: Genesis
  - **Chapters/Verses**: Genesis 4:1-16
  - **Description**: The story of the first murder, in which Cain kills his brother Abel out of jealousy after God favored Abel's offering.

- [Pentecost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentecost)
  - **Book(s)**: Acts of the Apostles
  - **Chapters/Verses**: Acts 2:1-31
  - **Description**: The descent of the Holy Spirit upon the apostles fifty days after Easter, enabling them to speak in tongues and marking the birth of the Church.

- [Marriage at Cana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage_at_Cana)
  - **Book(s)**: Gospel of John
  - **Chapters/Verses**: John 2:1-11
  - **Description**: Jesus's first miracle, turning water into wine at a wedding feast in Cana of Galilee.

## Gallerie dell'Accademia, Venice

<!-- Last updated: 2026-02-04 -->

- [Gallerie dell'Accademia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallerie_dell'Accademia)
  - **Type**: Museum
  - **Description**: A museum gallery of pre-19th-century art in Venice housing the world's best collection of Venetian School paintings. Located in the former Scuola della Carità on the south bank of the Grand Canal in Dorsoduro. Contains over 500 works spanning the Byzantine and Gothic periods through the Renaissance and Baroque eras.

### Artworks

- [Vitruvian Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitruvian_Man)
  - **Artist**: [Leonardo da Vinci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_da_Vinci)
  - **Medium**: Pen and ink on paper
  - **Date**: c. 1490
  - **Description**: A drawing depicting a nude man in two superimposed positions inscribed within a circle and square, illustrating ideal human proportions as described by the Roman architect Vitruvius. Justly ranked among the all-time iconic images of Western civilization. Due to its fragility, displayed only every 4-6 years.
  ![img](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/22/Da_Vinci_Vitruve_Luc_Viatour.jpg)

- [The Tempest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tempest_(Giorgione))
  - **Artist**: [Giorgione](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgione)
  - **Medium**: Oil on canvas
  - **Date**: 1506-1508
  - **Description**: A mysterious Renaissance painting originally commissioned by Venetian noble Gabriele Vendramin. Depicts a soldier and a nursing woman in a lush landscape with a city threatened by a storm. Despite considerable scholarly discussion, the meaning remains elusive. Considered by some the first true landscape in Western art.
  ![img](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/8a/Giorgione_-_Das_Gewitter.jpg)

- [The Feast in the House of Levi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Feast_in_the_House_of_Levi)
  - **Artist**: [Paolo Veronese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Veronese)
  - **Medium**: Oil on canvas
  - **Date**: 1573
  - **Description**: One of the largest canvases of the 16th century (555 x 1,309 cm). Originally painted as a Last Supper for a Dominican friary, Veronese's irreverent interpretation led to an investigation by the Inquisition. Rather than make changes, he simply renamed the painting. A masterpiece of Venetian colorism.
  ![img](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/48/The_Feast_in_the_House_of_Levi_by_Paolo_Veronese_%28edited_2%29.jpg)

- [Pieta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piet%C3%A0_(Titian))
  - **Artist**: [Titian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian)
  - **Medium**: Oil on canvas
  - **Date**: 1575-1576
  - **Description**: One of Titian's last paintings, left incomplete at his death in 1576 and finished by Palma Giovane. Titian intended it for his own grave. A profoundly moving late work demonstrating the artist's loose, expressive brushwork in his final years.
  ![img](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/59/Accademia_-_Piet%C3%A0_by_Titian.jpg)

- [The Presentation of the Virgin at the Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Presentation_of_the_Virgin_at_the_Temple_(Titian))
  - **Artist**: [Titian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian)
  - **Medium**: Oil on canvas
  - **Date**: 1534-1538
  - **Description**: A huge painting (335 x 775 cm) depicting the three-year-old Virgin Mary entering the Temple of Jerusalem. Commissioned for the Scuola della Carita and still in its original location, now incorporated into the museum.
  ![img](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/02/Tiziano%2C_presentazione.jpg)

- [San Giobbe Altarpiece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Giobbe_Altarpiece)
  - **Artist**: [Giovanni Bellini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovanni_Bellini)
  - **Medium**: Oil on panel
  - **Date**: c. 1487
  - **Description**: A sacra conversazione inspired by a plague outbreak in 1485, originally designed in situ with the architecture of the Church of San Giobbe. Shows the Madonna and Child with Saints Francis, John the Baptist, Job, Dominic, Sebastian, and Louis. One of the largest sacra conversazione paintings of its time.
  ![img](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/aa/Accademia_-_Pala_di_San_Giobbe_by_Giovanni_Bellini.jpg)

- [Procession in St. Mark's Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Procession_in_St._Mark's_Square)
  - **Artist**: [Gentile Bellini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gentile_Bellini)
  - **Medium**: Tempera on canvas
  - **Date**: c. 1496
  - **Description**: Part of a cycle depicting miracles of the True Cross, this large canvas provides a remarkable view of Piazza San Marco in the 15th century, showing the old mosaics on the basilica facade and contemporary Venetian life in extraordinary detail.
  ![img](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/44/Accademia_-_Procession_in_piazza_San_Marco_by_Gentile_Bellini.jpg)

- [Miracle of the Relic of the Cross at the Ponte di Rialto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miracle_of_the_Relic_of_the_Cross_at_the_Ponte_di_Rialto)
  - **Artist**: [Vittore Carpaccio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vittore_Carpaccio)
  - **Medium**: Tempera on canvas
  - **Date**: c. 1496
  - **Description**: Also known as The Healing of the Madman, this painting depicts a miracle of the True Cross relic, showing the old wooden Rialto Bridge and providing invaluable documentation of 15th-century Venetian architecture and daily life.
  ![img](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9d/Accademia_-_Miracle_of_the_Holy_Cross_at_Rialto_by_Vittore_Carpaccio.jpg)

- Legend of Saint Ursula Cycle
  - **Artist**: [Vittore Carpaccio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vittore_Carpaccio)
  - **Medium**: Tempera on canvas
  - **Date**: 1490-1495
  - **Description**: A cycle of nine large paintings commissioned by the Loredan family depicting the legend of Saint Ursula and her eleven thousand virgin martyrs. Notable for detailed depictions of architecture, nature, and contemporary Venetian life. Includes famous scenes such as The Dream of Saint Ursula.

### Artists

- [Leonardo da Vinci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_da_Vinci)
  - **Born**: 1452, Vinci
  - **Died**: 1519, Amboise
  - Italian polymath of the High Renaissance who was active as a painter, draughtsman, engineer, scientist, theorist, sculptor, and architect. Widely regarded as a genius who epitomized the Renaissance humanist ideal.

- [Giorgione](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgione)
  - **Born**: c. 1477, Castelfranco Veneto
  - **Died**: 1510, Venice
  - Giorgio Barbarelli da Castelfranco, known as Giorgione, was a Venetian painter of the High Renaissance known for the elusive poetic quality of his work. Only about six surviving paintings are firmly attributed to him, making him one of the most mysterious figures in European art.

- [Gentile Bellini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gentile_Bellini)
  - **Born**: c. 1429, Venice
  - **Died**: 1507, Venice
  - Venetian painter from Venice's leading family of painters. From 1474, he was the official portrait artist for the Doges of Venice. Known for large works with multitudes of figures, especially for the Scuole Grandi of Venice.

- [Vittore Carpaccio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vittore_Carpaccio)
  - **Born**: c. 1465, Venice
  - **Died**: 1525/1526, Venice
  - Italian painter of the Venetian school who studied under Gentile Bellini. Known for his command of perspective, precise attention to architectural detail, and bold use of color. Many works display religious themes and cross-cultural elements.

### Bible Stories

- [Presentation of Mary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation_of_Mary)
  - **Book(s)**: Protoevangelium of James (apocryphal)
  - **Description**: According to tradition, Mary was presented at the Temple in Jerusalem at age three, where she was dedicated to God and lived until her betrothal. A popular subject in Renaissance art.

- [Pieta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piet%C3%A0)
  - **Book(s)**: Gospels (implied)
  - **Description**: The scene of the Virgin Mary mourning over the body of Christ after the Crucifixion. Though not described in the Gospels, it became one of the most moving subjects in Christian art.

- [Last Supper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last_Supper)
  - **Book(s)**: Matthew, Mark, Luke, John
  - **Chapters/Verses**: Matthew 26:17-30, Mark 14:12-26, Luke 22:7-38, John 13:1-30
  - **Description**: Jesus's final meal with his apostles before his crucifixion, during which he instituted the Eucharist. The original subject of Veronese's Feast in the House of Levi.
